candidates.title: GitHub separates Copilot trace identity from content capture
candidates.summary: GitHub added opt-in user and machine attribution to Copilot OpenTelemetry and split sensitive content collection into separately managed prompt, response, tool-argument, tool-output, and policy-detail classes.
candidates.what_changed: Copilot enterprise telemetry can now attribute activity to an authenticated GitHub login, operating-system account, and machine while leaving content disabled; administrators can independently control five sensitive content classes instead of relying only on the legacy all-content shorthand.
candidates.why_it_matters: Engineering organizations can investigate agent reliability and accountability without automatically collecting source-bearing prompts and tool payloads, but identity plus repository and session metadata still creates a sensitive activity record that needs explicit access, retention, and routing policy.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Begin with metadata-only traces, enable identity only for an approved attribution need, treat each content class as a separate sensitive data source, route OTLP to a restricted collector, and test the effective managed policy on every deployed client surface.

evidence.rationale: GitHub's dated changelog and current GitHub and VS Code documentation define the settings, fields, defaults, precedence, supported trace contents, and data-sensitivity warnings.
evidence.independent_validation: No independent audit or cross-client implementation test of the new capture controls was found.
evidence.claim_scope: The story reports the documented control surface and its operational implications; it does not claim uniform implementation across all clients or compliance sufficiency.

signal.rationale: The update changes how enterprises can balance agent accountability, observability, and collection of source-bearing or identity-bearing data across managed coding-agent clients.

learning_gap.existing_explainer_status: Pulse has a September briefing on Copilot OpenTelemetry export, but no reusable explainer on the difference between trace metadata, identity, and content capture for coding agents.
learning_gap.suggested_explainer: What an AI Agent Trace Can Reveal

follow_up_opportunities.reason: The independent capture classes support a concrete deployment checklist for metadata-only baselines, audited identity enablement, temporary content escalation, collector controls, redaction, and retention.

deduplication.canonical_event: GitHub adds identity attribution and five independently managed content-capture classes to Copilot OpenTelemetry on October 12, 2026.
deduplication.material_delta: The September story covered initial OpenTelemetry export and a single content-capture boundary. The new release adds opt-in user, OS-account, and host attribution and separates prompts, responses, tool arguments, tool output, and policy detail into independently controlled capture classes with managed-setting precedence.

publication_verification.notes: The October 12 changelog and current GitHub and VS Code references were rechecked. All settings and sensitive-data descriptions remain first-party documentation; no independent audit was located.

watchlist.title: Aptos bundles MCP, agent skills, and LLM-ready docs for Move development
watchlist.summary: Aptos documentation now presents an official MCP server, installable Move and TypeScript SDK skills, and llms.txt feeds as one AI-assisted development surface.

evidence.rationale: The official documentation exposes installation paths and the combined tool surface, while dated secondary coverage identifies the October update.

signal.rationale: The bundle is a useful domain-specific agent-tooling pattern, but its security model, versioning, evaluation results, and adoption are not yet documented well enough for selection.

watchlist.reason: The integrated surface is real, but the primary documentation does not provide a dated release record, threat model, versioning contract, or measured evidence that the combination improves correctness for Move development.
promote_when: A dated official release or repository tag defines the MCP and skill versions and supported clients.
A security review, reproducible benchmark, or first-hand deployment documents correctness and permission behavior.

watchlist.title: Cloudflare's Skills-over-MCP release still awaits interoperability evidence
watchlist.summary: Cloudflare's API MCP server exposes skills through skills/list and skill:// resources, but the wider client and trust contract remains unsettled.

evidence.rationale: Cloudflare documents the endpoint and discovery/read mechanism.

signal.rationale: Remote skill discovery could standardize capability distribution, but practical interoperability and lifecycle controls remain unproven.

watchlist.reason: No new cross-client adoption, provenance, version-pinning, update-review, or permission evidence was found after the October 12 watch decision.
promote_when: Multiple independent MCP clients document interoperable Skills-over-MCP support.
Stable provenance, versioning, update, and permission guidance or a first-hand deployment documents those controls.
